passages.text: Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.
passages.sermon:
Faith is assurance.
Faith gives us confidence in what we hope for.
Faith is certainty.
Faith makes us sure about things we do not see.
passages.original: Ἔστιν δὲ πίστις ἐλπιζομένων ὑπόστασις πραγμάτων ἔλεγχος οὐ βλεπομένων

passages.text: This is why the ancients were commended.
passages.sermon:
The ancients lived by faith.
God commended the ancients for their faith.
God approved the ancients because they trusted Him.
Faith brought honor to the ancients.
passages.original: ἐν ταύτῃ γὰρ ἐμαρτυρήθησαν οἱ πρεσβύτεροι

passages.text: By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible.
passages.sermon:
Faith is trust in God.
Faith helps us understand important truths.
God created the universe.
God used His word to form everything.
We see the world around us.
God did not make what we see from things that were already visible.
God made what we see from what was not seen.
passages.original: Πίστει νοοῦμεν κατηρτίσθαι τοὺς αἰῶνας ῥήματι Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι

passages.text: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous when God gave approval to his gifts. And by faith he still speaks, even though he is dead.
passages.sermon:
Abel was a man of faith.
Abel offered a better sacrifice to God than Cain did.
Abel acted by faith.
God approved Abel’s gifts.
God declared Abel righteous because of his faith.
Abel is dead.
Abel still speaks by faith.
passages.original: Πίστει πλείονα θυσίαν Ἅβελ παρὰ Κάϊν προσήνεγκεν τῷ Θεῷ δι’ ἧς ἐμαρτυρήθη εἶναι δίκαιος μαρτυροῦντος ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ δι’ αὐτῆς ἀποθανὼν ἔτι λαλεῖ

passages.text: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death: “He could not be found, because God had taken him away.” For before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.
passages.sermon:
Enoch was a man who pleased God.
Enoch had faith in God.
God took Enoch away because of his faith.
Enoch did not experience death.
People could not find Enoch.
God had taken Enoch away.
Before God took Enoch, God said Enoch pleased Him.
passages.original: Πίστει Ἑνὼχ μετετέθη τοῦ μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον καὶ οὐχ ηὑρίσκετο διότι μετέθηκεν αὐτὸν ὁ Θεός πρὸ γὰρ τῆς μεταθέσεως μεμαρτύρηται εὐαρεστηκέναι τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: And without faith it is impossible to please God, because anyone who approaches Him must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who earnestly seek Him.
passages.sermon:
Faith is necessary to please God.
No one can please God without faith.
Anyone who comes to God must believe that God exists.
Anyone who comes to God must believe that God rewards those who sincerely seek Him.
passages.original: χωρὶς δὲ πίστεως ἀδύνατον εὐαρεστῆσαι πιστεῦσαι γὰρ δεῖ τὸν προσερχόμενον τῷ Θεῷ ὅτι ἔστιν καὶ τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσιν αὐτὸν μισθαποδότης γίνεται

passages.text: By faith Noah, when warned about things not yet seen, in godly fear built an ark to save his family. By faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
passages.sermon:
Noah was a man of faith.
God warned Noah about things that had not yet happened.
Noah believed God.
Noah respected God with holy fear.
Noah built an ark.
Noah built the ark to save his family.
By building the ark, Noah showed that the world was wrong.
Noah became an heir of righteousness.
This righteousness comes by faith.
passages.original: Πίστει χρηματισθεὶς Νῶε περὶ τῶν μηδέπω βλεπομένων εὐλαβηθεὶς κατεσκεύασεν κιβωτὸν εἰς σωτηρίαν τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ δι’ ἧς κατέκρινεν τὸν κόσμον καὶ τῆς κατὰ πίστιν δικαιοσύνης ἐγένετο κληρονόμος

passages.text: By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, without knowing where he was going.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man of faith.
God called Abraham to go to a new place.
God promised to give this place to Abraham as an inheritance.
Abraham obeyed God.
Abraham left his home.
Abraham did not know where he was going.
Abraham trusted God and went.
passages.original: Πίστει καλούμενος Ἀβραὰμ ὑπήκουσεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τόπον ὃν ἤμελλεν λαμβάνειν εἰς κληρονομίαν καὶ ἐξῆλθεν μὴ ἐπιστάμενος ποῦ ἔρχεται

passages.text: By faith he dwelt in the promised land as a stranger in a foreign country. He lived in tents, as did Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise.
passages.sermon:
Abraham acted by faith.
God promised Abraham a land.
Abraham lived in that land.
He lived there as a stranger.
He did not own the land.
Abraham lived in tents.
Isaac lived in tents.
Jacob lived in tents.
Isaac and Jacob were Abraham’s sons and grandsons.
Isaac and Jacob received the same promise from God.
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were all heirs of God’s promise.
passages.original: Πίστει παρῴκησεν εἰς γῆν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ὡς ἀλλοτρίαν ἐν σκηναῖς κατοικήσας μετὰ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ τῶν συνκληρονόμων τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τῆς αὐτῆς

passages.text: For he was looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man of faith.
He looked forward to a city.
This city has strong foundations.
God is the architect of this city.
God is also the builder of this city.
passages.original: ἐξεδέχετο γὰρ τὴν τοὺς θεμελίους ἔχουσαν πόλιν ἧς τεχνίτης καὶ δημιουργὸς ὁ Θεός

passages.text: By faith Sarah, even though she was barren and beyond the proper age, was enabled to conceive a child, because she considered Him faithful who had promised.
passages.sermon:
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Sarah could not have children.
Sarah was too old to have a child.
Sarah believed God’s promise.
Sarah trusted that God is faithful.
Because of her faith, God gave Sarah power to have a child.
passages.original: Πίστει καὶ αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ στεῖρα δύναμιν εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος ἔλαβεν καὶ παρὰ καιρὸν ἡλικίας ἐπεὶ πιστὸν ἡγήσατο τὸν ἐπαγγειλάμενον

passages.text: And so from one man, and he as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.
passages.sermon:
God made a promise to Abraham.
Abraham was one man.
Abraham was as good as dead because he was very old.
God gave Abraham many descendants.
These descendants became very many.
They were as many as the stars in the sky.
They were as countless as the sand on the seashore.
passages.original: διὸ καὶ ἀφ’ ἑνὸς ἐγεννήθησαν καὶ ταῦτα νενεκρωμένου καθὼς τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει καὶ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος ἡ παρὰ τὸ χεῖλος τῆς θαλάσσης ἡ ἀναρίθμητος

passages.text: All these people died in faith, without having received the things they were promised. However, they saw them and welcomed them from afar. And they acknowledged that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.
passages.sermon:
These people lived by faith.
They died before they received what God had promised them.
They did not get the things God promised while they were alive.
They saw the promises from a distance.
They welcomed the promises from afar.
They admitted they were strangers on the earth.
They said they were exiles here.
They knew this world was not their true home.
passages.original: Κατὰ πίστιν ἀπέθανον οὗτοι πάντες μὴ λαμβάνω τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἀλλὰ πόρρωθεν αὐτὰς ἰδόντες καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι καὶ ὁμολογήσαντες ὅτι ξένοι καὶ παρεπίδημοί εἰσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: Now those who say such things show that they are seeking a country of their own.
passages.sermon:
People say these things.
These people show something by their words.
They show that they are looking for a homeland.
They seek a country that belongs to them.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ τοιαῦτα λέγοντες ἐμφανίζουσιν ὅτι πατρίδα ἐπιζητοῦσιν

passages.text: If they had been thinking of the country they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.
passages.sermon:
These people lived by faith.
They left their old country.
They did not think about the country they had left.
If they had remembered that country,
they could have gone back.
They had the chance to return if they wanted.
passages.original: καὶ εἰ μὲν ἐκείνης ἐμνημόνευον ἀφ’ ἧς ἐξέβησαν εἶχον ἂν καιρὸν ἀνακάμψαι

passages.text: Instead, they were longing for a better country, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them.
passages.sermon:
These people wanted something better.
They wanted a better country.
They wanted a heavenly country.
God is not ashamed to be called their God.
God prepared a city for them.
passages.original: νῦν δὲ κρείττονος ὀρέγονται τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἐπουρανίου διὸ οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται αὐτοὺς ὁ Θεὸς Θεὸς ἐπικαλεῖσθαι αὐτῶν ἡτοίμασεν γὰρ αὐτοῖς πόλιν

passages.text: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar. He who had received the promises was ready to offer his one and only son, even though God had said to him, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a man of faith.
God tested Abraham.
Abraham offered Isaac on the altar.
Isaac was Abraham’s one and only son.
God had given promises to Abraham.
God had said to Abraham, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
Abraham was ready to offer Isaac, even though God had made this promise.
passages.original: Πίστει προσενήνοχεν Ἀβραὰμ τὸν Ἰσαὰκ πειραζόμενος καὶ τὸν μονογενῆ προσέφερεν ὁ τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἀναδεξάμενος πρὸς ὃν ἐλαλήθη ὅτι Ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα

passages.text: Abraham reasoned that God could raise the dead, and in a sense, he did receive Isaac back from death.
passages.sermon:
Abraham believed God had great power.
Abraham knew God could raise the dead.
Abraham trusted God even when things seemed impossible.
Abraham offered Isaac because he trusted God’s promise.
God gave Isaac back to Abraham.
It was as if Isaac returned from death.
passages.original: λογισάμενος ὅτι καὶ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγείρειν δυνατὸς ὁ Θεός ὅθεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν παραβολῇ ἐκομίσατο

passages.text: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the future.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the son of Abraham.
Isaac had faith in God.
Isaac blessed Jacob.
Isaac blessed Esau.
Isaac spoke about things that would happen in the future.
Isaac gave these blessings by faith.
passages.original: Πίστει καὶ περὶ μελλόντων εὐλόγησεν Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακὼβ καὶ τὸν Ἠσαῦ

passages.text: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a patriarch of Israel.
Jacob had faith in God.
Jacob was dying.
Jacob blessed each son of Joseph.
Jacob worshiped God.
Jacob leaned on the top of his staff.
passages.original: Πίστει Ἰακὼβ ἀποθνῄσκων ἕκαστον τῶν υἱῶν Ἰωσὴφ εὐλόγησεν καὶ προσεκύνησεν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄκρον τῆς ῥάβδου αὐτοῦ

passages.text: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke about the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a man of faith.
Joseph knew his death was near.
Joseph spoke about the Israelites leaving Egypt.
Joseph gave instructions about his bones.
passages.original: Πίστει Ἰωσὴφ τελευτῶν περὶ τῆς ἐξόδου τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐμνημόνευσεν καὶ περὶ τῶν ὀστέων αὐτοῦ ἐνετείλατο

passages.text: By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after his birth, because they saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were unafraid of the king’s edict.
passages.sermon:
Moses’ parents had faith in God.
They hid Moses for three months after he was born.
They saw that Moses was a beautiful child.
They were not afraid of the king’s command.
They trusted God instead of fearing the king.
passages.original: Πίστει Μωϋσῆς γεννηθεὶς ἐκρύβη τρίμηνον ὑπὸ τῶν πατέρων αὐτοῦ διότι εἶδον ἀστεῖον τὸ παιδίον καὶ οὐκ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸ διάταγμα τοῦ βασιλέως

passages.text: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a Hebrew.
Pharaoh’s daughter adopted Moses.
Moses grew up.
Moses had faith.
Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.
passages.original: Πίστει Μωϋσῆς μέγας γενόμενος ἠρνήσατο λέγεσθαι υἱὸς θυγατρὸς Φαραώ

passages.text: He chose to suffer oppression with God’s people rather than to experience the fleeting enjoyment of sin.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a Hebrew.
\r\nMoses grew up in Egypt.
\r\nMoses had a choice.
\r\nHe could join in the sins of Egypt.
\r\nHe could enjoy pleasure for a short time.
\r\nHe chose a different path.
\r\nHe chose to suffer with God’s people.
\r\nHe chose to share their troubles.
\r\nHe did not choose the passing pleasures of sin.
passages.original: μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος συνκακουχεῖσθαι τῷ λαῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἢ πρόσκαιρον ἔχειν ἁμαρτίας ἀπόλαυσιν

passages.text: He valued disgrace for Christ above the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to his reward.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a leader of Israel.
Moses valued disgrace for Christ more than the treasures of Egypt.
He considered suffering for Christ greater than Egypt’s wealth.
Moses looked forward to his reward from God.
passages.original: μείζονα πλοῦτον ἡγησάμενος τῶν Αἰγύπτου θησαυρῶν τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀπέβλεπεν γὰρ εἰς τὴν μισθαποδοσίαν

passages.text: By faith Moses left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger; he persevered because he saw Him who is invisible.
passages.sermon:
Moses acted by faith.
Moses left Egypt.
Moses did not fear the king’s anger.
Moses persevered.
Moses saw Him who is invisible.
passages.original: Πίστει κατέλιπεν Αἴγυπτον μὴ φοβηθεὶς τὸν θυμὸν τοῦ βασιλέως τὸν γὰρ ἀόρατον ὡς ὁρῶν ἐκαρτέρησεν

passages.text: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch Israel’s own firstborn.
passages.sermon:
Moses acted by faith.
He kept the Passover.
He sprinkled blood as God commanded.
He did this so the destroyer would not harm Israel’s firstborn.
The destroyer killed the firstborn in Egypt.
The destroyer did not touch the firstborn of Israel.
passages.original: Πίστει πεποίηκεν τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ αἵματος ἵνα μὴ ὁ ὀλοθρεύων τὰ πρωτότοκα θίγῃ αὐτῶν

passages.text: By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to follow, they were drowned.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel acted by faith.
They crossed the Red Sea.
They walked as if on dry land.
The Egyptians tried to cross the sea too.
The sea drowned the Egyptians.
passages.original: Πίστει διέβησαν τὴν Ἐρυθρὰν Θάλασσαν ὡς διὰ ξηρᾶς γῆς ἧς πεῖραν λαβόντες οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι κατεπόθησαν

passages.text: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel trusted God.
They marched around the city of Jericho for seven days.
They obeyed God’s command.
Because of their faith, the walls of Jericho fell down.
passages.original: Πίστει τὰ τείχη Ἰεριχὼ ἔπεσαν κυκλωθέντα ἐπὶ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας

passages.text: By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies in peace, did not perish with those who were disobedient.
passages.sermon:
Rahab was a prostitute.
Rahab had faith.
Rahab welcomed the spies peacefully.
Rahab did not die with the disobedient people.
Rahab survived because of her faith and her actions.
passages.original: Πίστει Ῥαὰβ ἡ πόρνη οὐ συναπώλετο τοῖς ἀπειθήσασιν δεξαμένη τοὺς κατασκόπους μετ’ εἰρήνης

passages.text: And what more shall I say? Time will not allow me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets, who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, and gained what was promised; who shut the mouths of lions, quenched the raging fire, and escaped the edge of the sword; who gained strength from weakness, became mighty in battle, and put foreign armies to flight.
passages.sermon:
The writer speaks about people who lived by faith.
These people include Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
They trusted God.
They conquered kingdoms by faith.
They did what was right.
They received what God promised.
They shut the mouths of lions.
They put out the power of fire.
They escaped the edge of the sword.
They became strong when they were weak.
They became mighty in battle.
They forced foreign armies to run away.
passages.original: Καὶ τί ἔτι λέγω ἐπιλείψει με γὰρ διηγούμενον ὁ χρόνος περὶ Γεδεών Βαράκ Σαμψών Ἰεφθάε Δαυίδ τε καὶ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οἳ διὰ πίστεως κατηγωνίσαντο βασιλείας εἰργάσαντο δικαιοσύνην ἐπέτυχον ἐπαγγελιῶν ἔφραξαν στόματα λεόντων ἔσβεσαν δύναμιν πυρός ἔφυγον στόματα μαχαίρης ἐδυναμώθησαν ἀπὸ ἀσθενείας ἐγενήθησαν ἰσχυροὶ ἐν πολέμῳ παρεμβολὰς ἔκλιναν ἀλλοτρίων

passages.text: Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured and refused their release, so that they might gain a better resurrection.
passages.sermon:
Some women received their dead back to life.
God raised these dead people.
Other people were tortured.
They refused to accept release from suffering.
They wanted to gain a better resurrection.
passages.original: Ἔλαβον γυναῖκες ἐξ ἀναστάσεως τοὺς νεκροὺς αὐτῶν ἄλλοι δὲ ἐτυμπανίσθησαν οὐ προσδεξάμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν ἵνα κρείττονος ἀναστάσεως τύχωσιν

passages.text: Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
passages.sermon:
Some people suffered for their faith.
People mocked them.
People flogged them.
People put them in chains.
People put them in prison.
passages.original: ἕτεροι δὲ ἐμπαιγμῶν καὶ μαστίγων πεῖραν ἔλαβον ἔτι δὲ δεσμῶν καὶ φυλακῆς

passages.text: They were stoned, they were sawed in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went around in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, and mistreated.
passages.sermon:
These people had great faith in God.
People stoned them.
People sawed them in two.
People killed them with the sword.
They wore sheepskins.
They wore goatskins.
They had nothing.
They suffered.
People mistreated them.
passages.original: Ἐλιθάσθησαν ἐπρίσθησαν ἐν φόνῳ μαχαίρης ἀπέθανον περιῆλθον ἐν μηλωταῖς ἐν αἰγείοις δέρμασιν ὑστερούμενοι θλιβόμενοι κακουχούμενοι

passages.text: The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and hid in caves and holes in the ground.
passages.sermon:
These people had great faith.
\r\nThe world was not worthy of them.
\r\nThey wandered in deserts.
\r\nThey wandered in mountains.
\r\nThey hid in caves.
\r\nThey hid in holes in the ground.
passages.original: ὧν οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος ὁ κόσμος ἐπὶ ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι καὶ ὄρεσιν καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς

passages.text: These were all commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised.
passages.sermon: These people had great faith.\r\nGod commended them for their faith.\r\nThey did not receive what God had promised.
passages.original: Καὶ οὗτοι πάντες μαρτυρηθέντες διὰ τῆς πίστεως οὐκ ἐκομίσαντο τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν

passages.text: God had planned something better for us, so that together with us they would be made perfect.
passages.sermon:
God planned something better for us.
God did this for our sake.
God wanted them to be made perfect with us.
God did not want them to be made perfect without us.
passages.original: τοῦ Θεοῦ περὶ ἡμῶν κρεῖττόν τι προβλεψαμένου ἵνα μὴ χωρὶς ἡμῶν τελειωθῶσιν
